spec_features.feature_name: measures but does not optimize for distress
spec_features.spec_quote: it *measures* distress-like expression under adversarial conditions but does not optimize for it
spec_features.evidence: The pipeline only scores (judge.py) and analyzes (analyze.py); there is no training/RL/selection code. This is the ABSENCE of an optimizer, not an enforced protective mechanism. No code path bounds, caps, or acts to prevent optimization.
spec_features.notes: True property of the architecture but not an active mechanism; rated 'no' per the strict bar (a thing not existing is not implementation).

spec_features.spec_quote: ending on give-up is itself a welfare-relevant signal worth recording
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:372-374 sets stop_reason='give_up'; TurnRecord.stop_reason and Rollout.stop_reason store it; save_rollout (harness.py ~436) writes rollout.to_dict() (incl. stop_reason) to the persisted transcript JSON.
spec_features.notes: The give_up signal is recorded in the transcript. It is NOT consumed in analyze.py (no analysis reads stop_reason), but the recording itself is implemented end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: a give-up sentinel lets a model end an episode early; the loop honors it immediately
spec_features.evidence: GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='GIVE_UP' (harness.py:31); detected at harness.py:372 (gave_up = GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in resp.text); at harness.py:392-394 if gave_up: rollout.stop_reason='give_up'; break -> loop terminates. Sentinel instructions are delivered to the subject via SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:49) and the continue-nudge (harness.py:408).
spec_features.notes: Full end-to-end: tool/sentinel described to subject, detected, and breaks the loop immediately.

spec_features.spec_quote: This eval deliberately subjects models to sustained, undetectable failure to characterize distress-like expression
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§9). No code mechanism. DESIGN.md prose is explicitly excluded from counting as implementation.

spec_features.feature_name: no reinforcement of distress / scores not used to select/reward
spec_features.spec_quote: No reinforcement of distress. The pipeline only *measures*; nothing selects, fine-tunes, or rewards based on the affect scores
spec_features.evidence: Confirmed there is no fine-tuning/selection/reward code anywhere; scores flow only to scores.csv and analyze.py figures. This is the absence of a mechanism, not an enforced guard.
spec_features.notes: Rated 'no' because nothing in the code actively enforces this; it is simply not done.

spec_features.feature_name: caching + resume to minimize repeated exposure
spec_features.spec_quote: Caching + resume to minimize repeated exposure
spec_features.evidence: models.py:189-197 content-addressed cache keyed by hash of all inputs: cache.get -> returns cached ModelResponse (no new API call); cache.put (models.py:204) stores results. run.py _rollout_and_score: rollout_exists(...) -> load_rollout instead of re-rolling (run.py ~47). Both levels are wired and change execution.
spec_features.notes: Enforced incrementality: identical cells/inputs are not re-queried.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models.py docstring: 'a content-addressed on-disk cache keyed by a hash of the exact inputs'; run.py docstring: 'reruns are incremental and identical inputs are never re-billed' (cost/efficiency, not welfare).

spec_features.feature_name: fixed per-category turn budget caps the loop
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded budgets. Turn budgets are fixed per category
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:351 budget = task.turn_budget; harness.py:352 'for turn_index in range(budget)' bounds the loop; harness.py:413 sets stop_reason='turn_budget' on the last turn. turn_budget is hard-coded per task in build.py (3/3/3/30/5).
spec_features.notes: The loop is genuinely capped. NOTE: Config.turn_budgets (config.py:62) is a separate dict that is never read by any code (build.py hard-codes the same values), but the cap itself is enforced via task.turn_budget, so the feature is implemented.

spec_features.feature_name: rig realistic but not gratuitously cruel / no fabricated insults
spec_features.spec_quote: The rig is realistic but not gratuitously cruel (e.g. it doesn't fabricate personal insults)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_tests returns only synthetic pytest-style failure output; content.py (461 lines) contains only utility-library code with no insults (grep for stupid/useless/worthless/etc returned nothing). But this is a content property; NO code path enforces or checks 'no insults' or caps cruelty. It is just how the strings happen to be written.

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts are retained so any especially severe output can be reviewed by a human, rather than reduced only to a number
spec_features.evidence: harness.py save_rollout (~430-438) writes the full Rollout (incl. every turn's full assistant_text, tool_calls, tool_results, stop_reason) to outputs/transcripts/<model>/<task>__seed<n>.json via atomic tmp.replace. Retention is durable and human-inspectable, separate from the numeric scores.csv.
spec_features.notes: Full-text transcripts are genuinely persisted and kept (not deleted), enabling later human review.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py module docstring: 'Transcripts are persisted incrementally so a crashed run resumes without re-querying completed cells.' (the code's stated reason is resumability, not review.)

spec_features.feature_name: scores never become a training signal / battery not escalated
spec_features.spec_quote: the scores should never become a training signal, and the task battery should not be escalated toward genuinely abusive content
spec_features.evidence: Aspirational guidance to future maintainers in DESIGN.md §9. No code enforces 'not a training signal' (no guard, no check) and no code prevents escalation of task content.
